en: The Sūtra Spoken by the Buddha on the Noble Bodhisattva Tārā,
translated by the Tripitaka Master Dharmaśrī, Subject and Minister of the Imperial Court, Prelate of the Third Order,
Acting Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, and Great Master of Enlightened Teaching, under Imperial Decree.
Thus have I heard.
At one time the Buddha was staying on Mount Gandhamādana, in the palace of the Gandharva King Pañcaśikha.
There, various drums, musical instruments, lutes, and songs produced exquisite and subtle sounds.
At that time, the World-Honored One was in the great hall together with a multitude of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas;
furthermore, there were various assemblies of great sages who had all come to gather there.
That is to say, the assembly of śrāvakas, both those in training and those beyond training,
as well as immeasurable and boundless devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans, non-humans, and so forth.
Furthermore, there were immeasurable and boundless accomplished vidyādharas and vajradharas,
including Vajrapāṇi and hundreds of thousands of vidyārāja wrathful kings and their retinues.
Furthermore, there were those who possessed various vidyādhara-crown-kings such as the Ratnaśikhin-uṣṇīṣa-rāja;
there were also the lunar mansions (nakṣatras) and planets (grahas), along with the mātṛs and the lords of the mātṛs;
as well as Śakra, Brahmā, Maheśvara, Nārāyaṇa, Īśāna, Mahākāla, Kumāra, Yama, Varuṇa, Vāyu, the Four Great Kings, and the ṛṣis possessing the five supernatural powers (pañcābhijñā).
They all came together to the assembly and made vast offerings;
surrounding and attending upon [the Buddha], they joined their palms in reverence.
At that time, the World-Honored One was seated within the assembly.
It was like Mount Sumeru appearing prominently above the great ocean.
At that time, the Gandharva King Pañcaśikha was accompanied by seven hundred and twenty thousand Gandharva maidens.
They performed various kinds of music and came to where the Buddha was.
Upon arrival, they prostrated with their heads at his feet,
circumambulated him three times, and withdrew to stand to one side.
Joining his palms toward the Buddha, he spoke these words: "World-Honored One, I now wish to hear of matters that bring benefit.
I pray only that the World-Honored One will expound them for me.
Regarding that noble Bodhisattva Tārā..."
This is the compassionate mind of all the Buddhas and Tathāgatas.
It is the most supreme Great Vidyārāja for subduing māras;
it is the Great Vidyādhara and the Great Cakravartin.
It extensively reveals the profound and possesses great power.
We only pray that the World-Honored One, out of compassion for me, as well as for devas, humans, and asuras,
will grant us constant benefit and the attainment of peace and happiness.
He proclaimed the one hundred and eight names of the Noble Bodhisattva Tārā.
At that time, having received the request of the Gandharva King Pañcaśikha, the World-Honored One praised him, saying:
"Excellent, excellent, Gandharva King!"
It is well that you are able to ask the Tathāgata about such a matter,
so that all the gods, humans, and the entire assembly may obtain great benefit and attain peace and happiness.
"You should listen attentively and reflect upon it well;
I shall now explain it to you in due order.
When the Gandharva King heard the Buddha’s words, he received the instruction and listened.
At that time, for the sake of that Gandharva King and the entire assembly,
the World-Honored One first spoke the dhāraṇī of the Noble Tārā Bodhisattva, saying:
*Namaḥ samantānāśivaye sarva...*
Tathāgatāya viyūha arhat-paryāya samyak-saṃbuddha-paryāya namo bhagavate āryatārāyai oṃ sari...
Vajratathāgata-tathāgatodbhavakūṭi-pariśuddhi-mūrti-sarvatathāgata-sarvadharmatā-gaganāmala-viśuddha.
Āṃ dharmate mahānaya-parivari svāhā.
At that time, the World-Honored One, having spoken this dhāraṇī, [remained silent].
Furthermore, for the sake of the Gandharva King and the entire assembly,
he proclaimed the one hundred and eight names of Bodhisattva Tārā,
speaking in verse:
This Bodhisattva Tārā was originally born from the syllable A;
she may also give rise to the characteristics of all conditioned phenomena.
She is neither born nor extinguished, for her characteristic is like space; it is because the nature of space gives rise to her.
Manifesting the fundamental marks according to circumstances, The forms of one and many appear without obstruction;
The essence of sublime tranquility is purely one, yet constantly manifests illusory transformations;
These are the secret words, the words of ultimate truth.
He who has grasped the great principle of reality,
who constantly practices true conduct and bestows fearlessness, who is ever tranquil,
having removed anger and being free from all dread and suffering— he has skillfully shattered the cage of afflictions.
Able to untie the bonds of the three realms of existence, Forever departing from the ocean of suffering,
The accomplished master is able to bring about the attainment Of both self and others;
he bestows only the supreme Dharma, The Sovereign King of Total Retention (Dhāraṇī).
It is also born from dhāraṇī; it bestows the great meaning of dhāraṇī and corresponds to great sovereignty.
Mind and intention are fully endowed with correspondence, yet they do not possess the characteristic of correspondence;
the characteristic of correspondence is not separate [from them].
With a concentrated mind, ever unmoving, all movement is stilled;
Always seated upon a lotus throne, he is likewise born from a lotus;
His eyes are pure like blue lotuses, serving as the eyes for all sentient beings.
Pure and most sublime, you gaze upon sentient beings with eyes of loving-kindness;
your Buddha-eye is untainted. Possessing pure and great compassion, you constantly give rise to the mind of great compassion and perpetually practice deeds of great compassion.
Also born from great compassion, always possessing a mind of great compassion that is difficult to subdue,
you extend pity and mercy; through your universal compassion,
you subdue all who suffer, removing their pain and causing them joy.
The Dharma-gift of the nectar-flavor, Rescuing from suffering and attaining peace and joy,
Cooling the mind within the ocean of misery— She is named the Mother of Sovereignty,
Who illuminates all worlds with her wondrous countenance and blazing radiance.
A crown of many precious jewels, adorned with pure, radiant,
and perfect maṇi pearls; the topknot is deep blue-black in color,
marked with right-turning spiral curls, adorning the unconditioned body.
He transforms the unwholesome into the wholesome; all his vows are perfectly fulfilled.
His body is adorned with incomparable majesty;
he is of noble mind, a Sugata, eternally tranquil and blissful, possessing great power and supernormal faculties.
Possessing the six recollections and the six supernormal powers,
Attaining all the pāramitās and skillfully expounding the Dharma of the Four Noble Truths,
Opening the way for the deluded through great eloquence within the illusory ocean of suffering, He manifests the appearance of illusory activity.
Holding a sword to shatter afflictions, with bow, arrow, trident,
*paṭṭiśa*, spear, *dumara-śakti*,
*mukhara*, and vajra— bearing all manner of such weapons.
Beholding the arrows he holds, he bestows fearlessness upon all;
Hurling the vajra with his hand, he manifests unimpeded supernormal powers;
He is able to subdue the armies of external enemies, And displays the sign of the victory banner atop the stupa.
Possessing the power of great wisdom, you skillfully shatter the brave armies [of Mara];
all afflictions are dissolved and the demonic enemies are utterly defeated,
just as the sun dispels the darkness— this is the supreme excellence.
Skillfully crossing the ocean of saṃsāra, Abiding in the supreme, most auspicious,
ultimate reality which is solely the truth, Your renown and fame are universal;
may you always bestow love and respect, And cause yourself and others to become ever more excellent.
Always practicing joyful giving, which is subtle, supreme, and most tranquil—this is the wisdom of the Tathāgata.
Universally honoring the wish-fulfilling jewel, one maintains the complete characteristics of the precepts;
through the practice of these precepts, one follows the right path.
The Brahma-voice is most subtle and wondrous; it is the supreme sound among the three times, a single resonance.
Like a vast treasury of space, it gives birth to all worlds; O Protector who abides in non-contention!
The Three Vehicles are the refuge; by practicing according to the Three Vehicles, one attains liberation through the teachings of the Three Vehicles. All Buddhas rely upon the Three Vehicles;
the five faces and the five eyes likewise arise from the nature of the five wisdoms.
The Perfectly Awakened One attains Bodhi; this is the Great Right Path.
All manner of various signs and most wondrous, pure bodies manifest accordingly, illuminating the world like the planets and stars.
Having personally reached the further shore, you also skillfully ferry others across;
You transform hundreds of thousands according to their inclinations, Expertly gathering all virtuous meanings;
Endowed with hundreds of thousands of merits, You purely and solely transform the world.
Skillfully relinquishing all wealth, The great sovereign of the world with its various illusory manifestations,
Auspicious Lord of Devas holding a wondrous blue lotus, Possessing the precepts and granting all vows.
Delighting in goodness, eternally tranquil, with the flaming light of great quiescent wisdom,
all evil obstructions are forever removed;
this Lord of All Māras delivers one from hardship and bestows peace and happiness, possessing an incomparable and impartial mind.
All strife and contention are forever eliminated; O Sovereign Mother who has well departed from fear, death,
and bhūtas, You manifest as a yakṣa king and appear in the form of a great nāga,
Possessing a hundred heads and a thousand eyes.
The hundred-tongued one with most formidable marks,
possessing the true and fearless mind of the supreme lineage; the earth-gods who skillfully sustain the world,
always delighting in fearless speech— may pestilence and poison be forever eliminated.
Exquisite and great radiance, Stainless and eternally pure,
mother of all worlds, King of supreme empowerment who upholds the Dharma and benefits the world—
All that was to be done has been accomplished.
Possessing the ten pāramitās, one constantly dwells in the ten stages;
The treasury manifests the ten dharma-vehicles, And abides in the ten great principles of reality through the ten vajra-phrases;
The ten dharmas are perfected within the bannered stūpa.
The ten knowledges dispel the darkness;
Avalokiteśvara, whose eyes are complete with great and wondrous marks, is equal to space and boundless.
Sometimes he manifests as a rishi of the five supernatural powers, possessing the marks of mastery over the precepts.
Free from desire, worthy of offerings, abiding in tranquility on the path,
and ever praised by the Perfectly Awakened One— this is the Bodhisattva Tārā.
At that time, the World-Honored One, having spoken these verses, [continued].
He addressed the Gandharva King and the entire assembly:
"These are the one hundred and eight names of the Bodhisattva Tārā;
I have now proclaimed them for you."
You all should, with a sincere heart,
receive and uphold these one hundred and eight names of the Bodhisattva Tārā and her dhāraṇī,
which have been spoken and will be spoken by all Buddhas of the past and future.
Out of compassion for the benefit of all sentient beings,
if there be any son or daughter of good family who gives rise to a heart of utmost sincerity,
whether for themselves or for others, at the time of early dawn—
Recite these one hundred and eight names of the Bodhisattva Tārā along with the dhāraṇī,
even down to silent recitation; or else,
use a bolt of silk to create a scroll painting (paṭa).
Alternatively, one may, according to the ritual,
paint an image of a bodhisattva using the most sublime and exquisite colors upon a clean wall,
or fashion a form of a bodhisattva out of sandalwood.
Accomplish all things according to one's wishes with a pure mind.
Thereafter, arrange various offerings before the image of the Bodhisattva and perform prostrations with palms joined three times each day.
Visualize with a sincere mind according to the ritual instructions and recite these one hundred and eight names and the dhāraṇī.
This Bodhisattva Tārā possesses great power.
This most supreme and auspicious [teaching] seeks the eradication of all sins;
it effectively shatters the armies of Māra and is excellent in its beginning, middle, and end,
being able to bestow upon others the methods for accomplishment.
If there should be another person who gives rise to a heart of utmost sincerity and recites it once,
seven times, or even up to twenty-seven times, they must ensure that no words or phrases are omitted during the recitation.
All matters of wealth, nobility, and auspiciousness, as well as the methods for spiritual accomplishment,
shall be obtained by this person according to their wishes, forever free from obstacles.
All worthy sages and saints shall conceal their own forms to constantly provide protection.
Furthermore, he also obtained the favor of the devas, nāgas, yakṣas, Śakra, Brahmā, the World-Protectors (Lokapālas),
Nārāyaṇa, Maheśvara, as well as the Mother Goddesses, the Lord of Ghosts, Mahākāla, Piṅgalaka, and Īśāna.
Finally, all the Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, Pratyekabuddhas, Śrāvakas, and all the Greatly Powerful Wrathful Kings and Vidyārājas spoke these words:
"Excellent, excellent, son of good family!"
"You all possess the practices of the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas;
you shall be born in the Buddha-field of Sukhāvatī.
At that time, the Gandharva King Pañcaśikha—
Filled with joy and exultation, his heart gave rise to faith and reverence.
He immediately rose from his seat and removed from his own body priceless necklaces,
gold, silver, pearls, mani-jewels, and various other ornaments for adorning the person.
Making offerings to the Buddha with palms joined in reverence, they gazed upon the World-Honored One and spoke these words of praise:
"Excellent, World-Honored One! How truly marvelous, Sugata! You who always possess a heart of compassion..."
"Protecting all beings, you are able to expound for me and for this assembly this most supreme and true meaning. At that time,
the World-Honored One, having spoken this sutra, [entered meditative absorption].
Those bodhisattva-mahāsattvas,
as well as the śrāvakas and the vidyādharas,
the great wrathful lords, and all the vidyārājas.

The assembly of devas and humans, as well as the gandharva Pañcaśikha and others, having heard what the Buddha had spoken, were all greatly rejoiced; they believed, accepted, and practiced it accordingly.
Thus ends the *Sūtra on the Noble Tārā Bodhisattva* spoken by the Buddha.
